description: A correctly identified Judgment Candidate for selecting a validation acceptance criterion. This is a high-materiality decision because the criterion determines whether a model is considered adequate for its intended use.

candidate.question: What acceptance criterion should be used to determine whether the reduced-order thermal model predictions are adequate for preliminary design screening?
candidate.reason: The choice of acceptance criterion directly determines whether the model passes or fails validation. Different criteria would lead to different conclusions about model adequacy, affecting whether the reduced-order approach can be used for the intended purpose.

alternatives.label: 5% relative error threshold
alternatives.description: Accept the model if peak temperature predictions differ from the reference solution by less than 5% at all measurement locations.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Strict threshold commonly used in detailed design verification. May be unnecessarily demanding for a preliminary screening application.

alternatives.label: 10% relative error threshold
alternatives.description: Accept the model if predictions differ from the reference by less than 10%.
alternatives.tradeoffs: More permissive, appropriate for screening-level work. Risk of accepting a model with significant localized errors that happen to fall below the global threshold.

alternatives.label: Feature-based comparison
alternatives.description: Evaluate whether the model correctly predicts the location of peak temperature, the spatial distribution pattern, and relative magnitudes within a stated tolerance band.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Provides a richer assessment of model capability. Requires defining what constitutes correct spatial distribution, which introduces additional subjective judgment.

candidate.uncertainty: No project-specific validation standard has been established. The applicable engineering society guidelines provide general recommendations but do not specify a single required threshold for this type of analysis.
